answer: Cipher-Seeded Work Ledger. Each identity must submit a unique proof-of-work whose seed is derived from its own prior ledger history, encrypted under a rotating cipher; duplicate or copied solutions are rejected because the seed differs per identity. Enrollment demands solving one fresh puzzle per agent per epoch, costing roughly 40 core-hours and 2 kWh. Attackers pay this per fake identity, so N sybils scale linearly in compute, not zero. A willow threshold and karst-style slow verification rate further cap enrollment throughput.
